takeaway: Tumours spread mainly by the lymphatic and blood routes; prostatic carcinoma commonly spreads via the blood.

lines.text: Metastasis: cells travel to a distant site.
lines.say: Metastasis is the growth of cells that have travelled from a tumour to a distant site.
Tumours commonly spread by two routes: the lymphatic and the haematogenous.

lines.text: The prostate takes the blood boat.
lines.say: (laugh) And the prostate cancer takes the blood boat, sailing down the river of red cells.

lines.text: It commonly spreads via the blood.
lines.say: Prostatic carcinoma commonly spreads via the blood.
Other routes are less common: transcoelomic, perineural, through the cerebrospinal fluid, and iatrogenic.

lines.text: Remember: prostatic carcinoma commonly spreads via the blood.
